### Key Risks of Mixing Them

- **Worsened side effects:** Both substances can trigger dizziness, headaches, nausea, anxiety, and changes in heart rate or blood pressure.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESjwEBxCJF1zSDTqicFeUv1yOHgQLLKcLTamFhLn4tHO4PLsiYQOy7uXjk55eSTX_u0_7Zgo-txburX-2do2p4HTA3di-1u0Jxyf3jpJGvVXuiRYADzXxDfYKkrZhN343QZ_vU9UbUShuxYKqKnP5geFF2G7Hw_tM0-LSyKmpEUErcANtm4aAb3qr6auVkW08B3Q)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbwHEIkXXiAoZRPXUQ-IO38EiYgJZNc1LBDQzj_RZ6syI7b_m-WeZQqgL5y_rCJHCzG0i31nnBY1W3-LR80lYmGGKXWAlmKi_0PS7kFGuuUbGFbM15C3ESqVCZw7EVs6IJ_uJtZyNHAZjt9MDXgnrjg)
- **Masked intoxication:** Pseudoephedrine acts as a stimulant while alcohol is a depressant. Stimulant effects can hide how impaired you actually are, making it easier to drink too much and risk accidents or alcohol poisoning.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgAEBxCJF10Gi088QknXp7_4re7snAQX0G4ukeVP1CDHuNU7MoUz8fH4OmwLA1dJ0E04xLs60QMxeIicQxGeCaZoKEmf0gr7QFVbMCGJS5L7SNXAdbzUEnAPic0cGHp2j4shmZDCNK7rFYzbWBgO7Gz3DY6rnZeBtpDgb91g_WirjEA)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgAEBxCJF16176dbA_haGppfutpVouLEn_3DdgCwO0QjZX4F4aUuYQ18wNCDpFrMiansYi0LvvMpm9VRvgkDeZeUKY2dPIitkRK6R9-XKUxuWjrWCMIfvtRX4OM6FBu3UOnbmbqe8QptHGX8RO2AfZrPBqTYE_0l2xWjzmwNn6el-4w)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESjwEBxCJF1zSDTqicFeUv1yOHgQLLKcLTamFhLn4tHO4PLsiYQOy7uXjk55eSTX_u0_7Zgo-txburX-2do2p4HTA3di-1u0Jxyf3jpJGvVXuiRYADzXxDfYKkrZhN343QZ_vU9UbUShuxYKqKnP5geFF2G7Hw_tM0-LSyKmpEUErcANtm4aAb3qr6auVkW08B3Q)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmQEBxCJF14hHxnhuRjSM4mgR8c3N0NAtZIzElQoAVMMFb_drMdi0UTn7RjEB4l9U7nMT2-7LmeEEH6-P3VFtkDpmf6sEVswxKeeuvUJCv9N-Bc-eJDtqpm3K22taPDT-fYjTpRofD6KNbJeNXfyNWApWxI2f7FtEpz9zeCLcire5gj3KetVwJoKfI3HW3rl_SN4bSTZ-8lMQ54I)

items.text: Worsened side effects: Both substances can trigger dizziness, headaches, nausea, anxiety, and changes in heart rate or blood pressure. Masked intoxication: Pseudoephedrine acts as a stimulant while alcohol is a depressant. Stimulant effects can hide how impaired you actually are, making it easier to drink too much and risk accidents or alcohol poisoning. Worse congestion and slower recovery: Alcohol can weaken your immune system when you are fighting a cold or flu. If you have allergies, histamines in certain drinks can also make nasal congestion worse. Added risks in combination products: Many sinus or cold medications combine pseudoephedrine with pain relievers (like ibuprofen, naproxen, or acetaminophen) or antihistamines. Mixing those ingredients with alcohol raises the risk of stomach bleeding, liver strain, or heavy drowsiness.
